Solution 2 has the correct final answer. Its heuristic checks out: the spike-spreading mechanism gives $\tau_\varepsilon \approx \min\{(M/\varepsilon)^2, n^2\}$ on the cycle, and the tail bound $P(M>x)\le \min(1, nx^{-p})$ then yields $\mathbb E\tau_\varepsilon \lesssim n^{2/p} + n^{3-p}$ for $p<2$ and $n^{2/p}$ for $p\ge 2$. Solution 1 drops the rare huge-spike contribution, which dominates the expectation when $1\le p<2$, so $2/p$ is wrong there. Solution 3 reaches the same boxed answer, but its trailing "Final answer" line is corrupted, so Solution 2 is the cleaner choice. I have not verified the matching upper bound for all graphs or checked the source paper, so my confidence is moderate.

CHOICE: 2
CONFIDENCE: 3
